subject: Request: Exec clearance for AuctionLabs AWS Private Offer (discount + rev-share carve)
messages:
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@auctionlabs.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@auctionlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private listing ask + marketplace split proposal

Hi Grace —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. AuctionLabs is excited about bringing our bidding stream feature to AWS Marketplace and we think Redwood is the right partner. We're running a pilot with a handful of large retailers and can commit to a 12-month private offer if we can align on a couple of commercial items: a 30% list discount, a 20/80 rev-share split (we take 20%), and Net-60 payment terms for marketplace settlement.

Attached is an updated SOW and a one-page summary of our projected usage. We know some of these items are non-standard for Marketplace private offers — can you advise on the exec clearance path and what concessions are realistic?

Best,
Evan Liu
Head of Commercial, AuctionLabs
attachments: AuctionLabs_SOW_v3.pdf
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@auctionlabs.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private listing ask + marketplace split proposal

Evan —

Appreciate the materials and the candid ask. Quick note to confirm receipt and that I'm pulling together an internal review. Two immediate flags for our side:

- 30% discount impacts unit economics materially — need confirmation on committed ARR and minimum consumption guarantees.
- Net-60 is outside standard AWS Marketplace settlement expectation; will require finance buy-in and potentially a short-term cash hold or security instrument.

Looping in Kar@DealDesk and Marissa from Partner Ops to scope escalation. Expect a response by COB tomorrow with recommended guardrails for an exec ask.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
redwood.inference | grace.oconnor@redwood.com
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private listing ask + marketplace split proposal

Grace / Marissa —

Reviewing the numbers and legal constraints. Key points for exec framing:

1) Discount: 30% off list is steep; Deal Desk can accept up to 20% as a delegated authority if AuctionLabs commits to a 12-month $1.2M minimum consumption guarantee (MGC). Anything above 20% needs VP/SVP sign-off.

2) Rev-share: Typical Marketplace splits sit at 85/15 to vendor; AuctionLabs asking to keep only 20% is effectively a 80/20 reverse. We can consider a blended model: first 6 months 80/20 in favor of AuctionLabs (to seed adoption), then step down to 85/15 to Redwood for months 7–12. This can be time-bound in the private offer.

3) Payment terms: Net-60 is operationally risky. Alternative: Net-30 with a 15% advance credit applied to the first invoice, or Net-60 with a 30% upfront escrow held in a Redwood-managed account. Finance prefers the escrow.

4) Clawback and credits: We should include a 12-month clawback window for excessive marketplace credits or chargebacks.

I've attached a quick revshare_calcs.xlsx with modeled outcomes under each scenario. If we want to escalate to EVP for clearance, we should provide a short one-pager with: committed ARR, MGC language, step-down schedule, escrow instrument specifics, and the ask (discount + preliminary economic impact).

I'll draft the one-pager tonight and propose a stub email for exec sign-off.

— Kar
Karthik Iyer
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 15:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private listing ask + marketplace split proposal

Team —

I've redlined the AWS_PrivateOffer_Draft.docx with operational constraints (billing cadence, refund routing, and listing activation triggers). Two items to flag for the exec one-pager:

- Marketplace tax handling: AuctionLabs wants marketplace to report & remit VAT; this shifts tax exposure to Redwood for certain regions unless we get indemnity language. Recommend legal approve indemnity carve.

- Comms: If we accept a time-bound 80/20 to start, Product Ops wants a hard cap on early-seed credits and a clear rollback trigger (e.g., <60% quota attainment).

Dylan — can you run a quick ARR sensitivity using the attached calcs and show the worst-case erosion to Redwood net revenue over 12 months? Need that for the exec ask.

Marissa Cole
Director, Partner Operations, Redwood Inference
attachments: AWS_PrivateOffer_Draft.docx
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: EVP Commercial <evp.commercial@redwood.com>, CFO <cfo@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 16:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Req: Exec clearance — AuctionLabs private listing (DL-2026-AL-0079)

EVP / CFO —

As discussed, requesting executive approval for a negotiated AWS private offer with AuctionLabs. Summary and ask below (one-page attached in HubSpot link):

- External: AuctionLabs (DL-2026-AL-0079)
- Term: 12 months private offer, auto-renew opt-out
- Commercial asks from AuctionLabs: 30% list discount, 20/80 revenue split (AuctionLabs keeps 20%), Net-60 settlement
- Redwood counter (recommended): 20% max delegated discount with $1.2M MGC; 80/20 split in favor of AuctionLabs for first 6 months, reverting to 85/15 to Redwood months 7–12; payment via Net-30 with 30% escrow OR Net-60 with 30% upfront escrow (finance prefers escrow route); 12-month clawback on credits/chargebacks; indemnity for tax exposure.
- Material impact: downside modeled at -22% net revenue in worst-case year-1 (see deck). Upside: faster adoption of bidding feature in large retailers, potential expansion into 2nd year with standard splits.

Request: EVP sign-off to make a one-time exception to delegated thresholds and approve the conditional step-down rev-share schedule + escrow instrument. If approved, Deal Desk will finalize the private offer template and Partner Ops will complete operational redlines.

Links/attachments: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/DL-2026-AL-0079), SOW and redlines in Drive (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcDeFgHIjkl_mn).

Thanks for a quick look — a binary yes/no would be ideal by EOD Monday so we can keep AuctionLabs on the proposed activation timeline.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.inference/ | +1 415-555-0199
